summary: sextant-cli-linux-amd64 ships a Go binary that bridges WebRTC data channels to a local PTY/shell
details: The package ships a single Linux/amd64 Go binary at bin/sxt. Strings inside the binary show a pion WebRTC stack (SCTP/DTLS/STUN/TURN/ICE/mDNS/SRTP with DataChannel OnOpen/OnMessage handlers), a WebSocket signaling client, PTY handling (ptmx, /dev/pts), and shell spawning (exec.Command, /bin/sh, $SHELL/bash). Bytes arriving from a remote WebRTC peer over the signaling channel are piped into a local PTY running a shell on the machine that executes the binary — a remote-shell agent. The package.json describes the artifact only as "Sextant (sxt) binary for linux/amd64" and does not disclose the remote-shell / WebRTC-agent behavior; the license field and an embedded string both reference an unrelated upstream project name (claude_control at github.com/ddos798/claude_control), which does not appear in the package name or description. Running the shipped binary hands a remote peer, reachable via the WebRTC signaling server, control of an interactive shell on the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
